text: Despite the literal meaning of its name, only three Austroasiatic branches are actually spoken in South Asia: Khasic, Munda, and Nicobarese.

title: Tai Loi language - Wikipedia
text: Hall (2017) reports that Tai Loi is a cover term meaning 'mountain Tai' in Shan, and refers to various Angkuic, Waic, and Western Palaungic languages rather than a single language or branch.

title: Tai-Loi - Max Planck Society
text: Tai Loi means ‘mountain Tai’ and is a cover term for multiple Palaungic groups in the area, some of which are Angkuic and some of which are Waic. Population information is not yet available for the other groups known as Tai Loi.

title: Tai Loi language - grokipedia.com
text: Unlike many Austroasiatic languages that rely on register (phonation contrasts), Tai Loi has developed a rudimentary tonal system with three tones, influenced by contact with tonal Tai languages like Tai Lue, particularly through borrowings that introduce glottalization and falling contours.

title: Austro-Asiatic Language Family - Structure & Dialects - MustGo
text: The Austro-Asiatic language family consists of 169 languages spoken in Southeast Asia, in countries located between China and Indonesia. A few are spoken to the west of this area in the Nicobar Islands and in India. The austro– part of the name comes from the Latin word for ‘south.’
